transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-29 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Location: Zoom (recorded)
Attendees: Alex Martinez (Redwood AE), Samira Khan (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Graystone CTO), Jon Reyes (Graystone ML), Priya Iyer (Graystone Product)

Summary: Quick discovery focused on model selection for Graystone's internal knowledge assistant and external customer support bot. Main constraints: bilingual EN/FR support, long-context for multi-doc synthesis (~25k tokens target), strong audit/compliance needs (SOC2, on-prem option), tool-calling to internal systems (ticketing, inventory). Discussed tradeoffs across Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments and candidate open models; agreed to run a performance POC and share security docs and benchmarks.

Topics: model comparison (open models), context length required, multilingual quality (EN/FR), tool-calling/function-calling support, deployment modes (hosted/dedicated/private/VPC), encryption/KMS, audit logs, pricing/latency tradeoffs.

[00:00] Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros?
[00:12] Maya: sure, I'm Maya, CTO at Graystone. we build a B2B supply chain analytics platform, and now we want an assistant for internal ops and a customer-facing support bot.
[00:20] Jon: Jon, ml eng. I'm owning evals and latency/cost modeling.
[00:24] Priya: Priya, product, focused on UX and success metrics.
[00:28] Alex: great, Samira from our infra/ops team will run the technical pieces. Samira?
[00:34] Samira: hi — hi. we'll cover hosting options, model fit, and how tool calling works in Redwood.

[01:05] Maya: quick context, we have two hard constraints: bilingual support english/french — high quality — and long context, we often stitch 10–12 documents per session, typically ~20–25k tokens. also strict audit requirements for interactions that touch customer data.
[01:28] Alex: ok, makes sense. so you're looking at open models primarily?
[01:32] Jon: yes, cost is big — we want open models we can run on Dedicated or Private if needed. but we'll evaluate Hosted first because it's fastest to iterate.

[02:00] Samira: a couple of quick clarifications: do you need streaming? how important is latency vs cost — e.g., sub-300ms token latency is expensive at scale.
[02:12] Maya: streaming for chat UX is nice but not mandatory; latency matters for internal agent workflows (<400ms preferred), customer-facing can tolerate up to 1s. cost target is tight — want to keep token unit economics below our benchmark.
[02:32] Priya: also tool calling a must — we need secure function calling to our ticketing API and inventory system, with RBAC and audit trails.

[03:05] Samira: good. Redwood supports function/tool calling and structured outputs. for security, we have Private (VPC + on-prem control plane) which gives you customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) and full audit logs; Dedicated gives isolated GPU pools and better predictability; Hosted is easiest to start.
[03:35] Jon: curious about KV cache and prefix caching, that could cut costs a lot if we reuse context for common queries. how does that interact with long context models?
[03:48] Samira: we do automatic prefix/KV cache at runtime; if you have repeated doc fragments we can cache to reduce tokens and GPU compute. with longer context models (32k) we still manage KV cache for generation steps to save cycles.

[04:25] Maya: model candidates — we did a quick bench internally: we like Llama-3 style families, Mistral variants, and a couple of 32k open models. but we aren't sure about multilingual perf for FR. any suggestions?
[04:40] Samira: for EN/FR you'd want to compare a 32k-capable model vs a 8k model with retrieval augmentation. Mistral-large/3B class often struggles a bit on FR vs finetuned Llama variants — but results vary. we'll propose two candidates: a 32k Llama-family variant and a Mistral-ish 16–32k candidate.
[04:58] Alex: also worth noting quantization options — 4-bit/8-bit to reduce footprint; Redwood Optimize can recommend quant profiles by workload.

[05:35] Jon: does Redwood host quantized versions for Hosted or is that a Dedicated/Private thing?
[05:40] Samira: we host pre-quantized variants for many open models in Hosted; Dedicated gives you control to pin model versions and custom quant. Private you can bring your own, we just surface the runtime.

[06:05] Priya: about tool calling — can we restrict which functions each model instance can call? we need strict RBAC at function level.
[06:13] Samira: yes, per-route RBAC and token-level policies; calls are logged in audit trails. for Private you can integrate with your SSO/SAML and KMS.

[07:00] Maya: what's the fallback behavior if capacity is constrained? e.g., if hosted taxed during peak.
[07:06] Alex: Redwood has smart routing: policy-based routing to cheaper variants or canary fallbacks; you can route by latency cost or region. documented SLOs differ by plan — Dedicated gives SLA-backed latency targets.

[07:40] Jon: we need to run some accuracy evals — we'll share a labeled FR/EN prompt set. what's the best way to attach that to a POC?
[07:48] Samira: share the prompt set and desired metrics (F1/ROUGE/qualitative) — we'll run model comparisons and produce a bench spreadsheet with cost/latency/quality. that helps decide Hosted vs Dedicated.

[08:20] Priya: curious about token accounting — do you charge for cached context tokens if we reuse them?
[08:26] Alex: we bill for input and output tokens; caching reduces compute cost but token accounting on the API still counts what you send. if you use prefix insertion server-side in Dedicated/Private you can reduce billed tokens. we can go into detail in the pricing doc.

[09:05] Maya: encryption — we need envelope encryption with customer KMS and HSM-backed keys. is that supported on Hosted?
[09:14] Samira: Hosted supports TLS in transit and encryption at rest, but customer-managed KMS/HSM is only available in Private; Dedicated supports bring-your-KMS options in some tiers. we'll include exact capabilities in the security pack.

[10:00] Jon: performance POC specifics: we want a throughput run with 2k typical prompts, and a long-context synthesis test with 25k prompt plus retrieval. what's realistic for scheduling?
[10:12] Samira: we can set up a 2-hour POC bench on Dedicated nodes or Hosted with reserved capacity. for long-context we may need model variants with 32k context — we'll prep instances. target the week of April 11 as Alex mentioned.

[11:00] (brief cross talk)
[11:20] Maya: region/residency — our EU customers require data residency in eu-west-1. can Hosted guarantee region placement?
[11:29] Alex: yes, Hosted can pin region for data residency; Private gives full control. you'll want Dedicated for hybrid compliance with SLA.

[12:00] Priya: how does Redwood Console surface regression alerts? we want to detect quality drops after model updates.
[12:08] Samira: Redwood Console supports evals and regression monitoring tied to prompt sets; alerts can be webhooked and tied to rollbacks/canary policies. you'll get token-level cost and latency breakdowns too.

[13:00] Jon: for multilingual evals, what's your tooling for automatic metrics? BLEU is noisy; we'll likely do a mix of automated metrics and human review.
[13:12] Samira: agree. we'll run automated metrics for a first cut and sample human ratings; we'll include the human review plan in the bench doc.

[14:00] (Maya asks about pricing thresholds)
[14:10] Alex: high level: Hosted per-token plus embedding fees; Dedicated is reserved monthly GPU capacity; Private is enterprise licensing plus infra. I'll send scenario examples.

[15:00] Priya: any known model we should avoid for FR?
[15:05] Samira: some trickle-down smaller models have lower FR coverage; we recommend candidate list that balances cost and quality.

[16:00] (Jon reads off traffic numbers)
[16:10] Jon: our peak is 120 reqs/s low-medium length, avg 600 tokens out/in; heavy long-context sessions are ~5% of traffic but very sensitive.
[16:24] Samira: that's useful — batching policies can be tuned to keep latency while saving cost on the bulk of traffic.

[17:05] Maya: we also need legal and procurement — SLA, data processing addenda, and standard indemnities.
[17:13] Alex: we'll include standard enterprise docs and a sample contract; legal often needs the security pack first.

[18:00] Priya: about tool calling latency — if the model calls our ticketing API mid-generation, do you buffer or stream events?
[18:10] Samira: function calls are synchronous or async depending on your flow; streaming is supported but you can configure fallbacks and timeouts per-route. all calls logged.

[19:00] Jon: anything we should benchmark specifically?
[19:04] Samira: latency per token, end-to-end RTT with function calls, cold start for KV cache, and throughput at 95th percentile.

[19:40] (short silence, then next steps recap)
[20:00] Alex: recap and owner assignments: Alex send security pack & pricing scenarios; Samira send bench template and model candidates; Jon share prompt set and traffic. Graystone to confirm POC week availability.
[20:20] Maya: okay we'll aim to have prompt set by 3/31 and confirm POC week by 4/4.
[20:30] Priya: thanks — excited to see the bench results.

[21:00] Alex: anything else?
[21:05] Maya: no, that's it. thanks.
[21:10] Alex: great, we'll follow up by email with attachments. bye.

(Recording ends)

Notes: transcription contains minor speaker attribution errors and common ASR mistakes; proper nouns like "K-V cache" occasionally spelled with hyphen; Redwood product names referenced informally as Redwood Console/Optimize/Private/Dedicated.
